name: Tadalafil BPH dose-finding trial
question: Does once-daily tadalafil improve lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia compared with placebo?

design.population: 1,058 men aged at least 45 years with at least six months of LUTS associated with clinical BPH; pre-run-in IPSS at least 13, Qmax 4–15 mL/s, and screening PVR below 300 mL.
design.locator: Full text, Study Design and Participants, p 1229; Figure 2, p 1231

verdictNote: The prespecified 5 mg IPSS comparison met its endpoint; 5 mg had the authors' preferred risk-benefit profile.
takeaway: In men with BPH-associated lower urinary tract symptoms, tadalafil 5 mg once daily improved IPSS by 4.87 versus 2.27 points with placebo after 12 weeks (P <0.001); 2.5, 10 and 20 mg also improved IPSS, without significant peak-flow differences.

delivery.label: Post hoc cohort and treatment schedule
delivery.value: 581 sexually active men with ED and BPH-LUTS entered the post hoc cohort; 579 contributed IIEF-EF efficacy data. Prior BPH/ED therapies required a four-week washout; all men had a four-week placebo run-in, then received placebo or tadalafil 2.5, 5, 10 or 20 mg once daily for 12 weeks. No minimum intercourse-attempt frequency was required.
delivery.locator: Full text, Patients and methods, pp 728–729; Results, p 730

delivery.label: Extension participation and completion
delivery.value: Of 886 randomized-period completers, 428 entered the 52-week open-label extension and 427 received tadalafil 5 mg once daily; 299/428 entrants (69.9%) completed it. No other BPH or ED drugs were permitted. Prior assignments among recipients were placebo 92, tadalafil 2.5 mg 96, 5 mg 83, 10 mg 85, and 20 mg 71.
